Chapter 3 Slides: Graphics (Albert, Baumer, Marchi)

Slide 1: Chapter Overview
Goal: Introduce graphical methods using ggplot2 in R

Dataset: Hall of Fame batting and pitching statistics

Sections:

- Visualizing categorical & numeric variables

- Creating and annotating plots

- Saving and exporting graphs

- Exploring hitting patterns and player comparisons

Slide 2: Section 3.1 - Introduction
- Use the hof_batting data to explore Hall of Fame hitters

- Remove pitchers to focus on 167 non-pitchers

- Learn to choose plots based on variable type (character vs numeric)

- Plot enhancement via + in ggplot2 for labels, styles, and annotations

Slide 3: Section 3.2 - Categorical Variables: Bar Plot
Add MidCareer and Era variables using mutate() and cut()

Frequency table via group_by() and summarize()

Bar plot using: ggplot(hof, aes(x = Era)) + geom_bar()

Insight: Most players are from the Lively Ball era

Slide 4: Section 3.2.2 - Adding Labels and Titles
Add axis titles with xlab() and ylab()

Add main title with ggtitle()

ggplot(hof, aes(Era)) + 
  geom_bar() +
  xlab("Baseball Era") +
  ylab("Frequency") +
  ggtitle("Era of the Nonpitching Hall of Famers")

Slide 5: Section 3.2.3 - Alternative Plot: Dot Plot
Build Cleveland-style dot plot with geom_point()

Flip coordinates with coord_flip() for clarity

ggplot(hof_eras, aes(Era, N)) + 
  geom_point(color = "red") + 
  coord_flip()

Slide 6: Section 3.3 - Saving Graphs
Save with ggsave("filename.png")
Export options: PNG, PDF, JPEG, etc.
Combine plots with patchwork library

p1 + p2; ggsave("graphs.pdf")

Slide 7: Section 3.4 - Numeric Variables: Scatterplot
One-dimensional scatterplot of OPS:


ggplot(hof, aes(x = OPS, y = 1)) + geom_jitter(height = 0.2)

Most OPS values fall between 0.7–1.0

Slide 8: Section 3.4 - Histogram
Basic histogram:
ggplot(hof, aes(x = OPS)) + geom_histogram()

Custom histogram:
ggplot(hof, aes(x = OPS)) + 
  geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0.4, 1.2, 0.1), color = "white", fill = "orange")

Slide 9: Section 3.5.1 - Two Numeric Variables
Scatterplot: OPS vs. MidCareer with smooth curve
ggplot(hof, aes(MidCareer, OPS)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth()

Pattern: Steady OPS, bump during 1930s

Slide 10: Section 3.5.1 - Label Outliers
Add player labels for outliers:
ggplot(hof, aes(MidCareer, OPS)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() +
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(hof, OPS > 1.05 | OPS < 0.5), aes(label = Player))


Slide 11: Section 3.5.2 - OBP vs SLG Graph
Initial plot:
p <- ggplot(hof, aes(OBP, SLG)) + geom_point()
Add axis labels:
p + xlab("On Base %") + ylab("Slugging %")


Slide 12: Section 3.5.2 - Add OPS Lines and Labels
Add OPS lines:
p + geom_abline(slope = -1, intercept = seq(0.7, 1.0, 0.1), color = "red")

Label OPS lines:
p + annotate("text", angle = -13, x = 0.31, y = 0.42, label = "OPS = 0.7")

Slide 13: Section 3.6 - Numeric & Factor: Stripchart
Add hr_rate = HR / AB
Parallel stripchart:
ggplot(hof, aes(hr_rate, Era)) + geom_jitter(height = 0.1)
Insight: Home runs increased post-Dead Ball era

Slide 14: Section 3.6.2 - Boxplot by Era
ggplot(hof, aes(Era, hr_rate)) + 
  geom_boxplot(color = "brown", fill = "orange") + 
  coord_flip()

Confirms: Babe Ruth as HR outlier

Slide 15: Section 3.7 - Comparing Ruth, Aaron, Bonds, A-Rod
Use Lahman People + Batting data
Create Age, cHR, group by Player
Plot:
ggplot(HR_data, aes(Age, cHR, color = Player)) + geom_line()


Slide 16: Section 3.8 - 1998 HR Race: McGwire vs Sosa
Extract play-by-play data from retro1998
Use cum_hr() to create date-wise HR counts

Final plot:
ggplot(hr_ytd, aes(Date, cumHR, color = nameLast)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 62)


Slide 17: Bonus Visualization - Spray Chart for Hits
Visualize where a player hits the ball
Use x/y coordinates from play-by-play data (if available)
ggplot(hit_data, aes(x = x_coord, y = y_coord)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) + 
  facet_wrap(~ batter_name)


Slide 18: Bonus Visualization - Heatmap of Home Run Zones
Use strike zone grid + home run rates
ggplot(zone_data, aes(plate_x, plate_z, fill = hr_rate)) + 
  geom_tile() + 
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red") + 
  coord_fixed()


Slide 19: Bonus Visualization - Animated Career Progression
Use gganimate to animate cumulative stats
ggplot(HR_data, aes(Age, cHR, color = Player)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  transition_reveal(Age)


Slide 20: Exercise 1 - Frequency Table & Bar Graph
hofpitching <- hof_pitching |>
  mutate(
    BF_group = cut(
      BF, 
      c(0, 10000, 15000, 20000, 30000),
      labels = c("Less than 10000", "(10000, 15000)", 
                 "(15000, 20000)", "more than 20000")
    )
  )
hofpitching |>
  group_by(BF_group) |>
  summarize(N = n())

Answer: 13 HOF pitchers faced more than 20,000 batters



Slide 21: Exercise 1 - Alternative Graph
ggplot(hofpitching, aes(BF_group)) + 
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") + 
  xlab("Batters Faced Group") + 
  ylab("Count") + 
  ggtitle("Distribution of Hall of Fame Pitchers by Batters Faced")

Alternative:
ggplot(hofpitching |>
  group_by(BF_group) |>
  summarize(N = n()), aes(N, BF_group)) +
  geom_point(color = "red") +
  ggtitle("Dot Plot of Pitchers by Batters Faced")


Slide 22: Exercise 2 - WAR Histogram
ggplot(hof_pitching, aes(WAR)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = "orange", color = "white")

Standout pitchers: Cy Young, Walter Johnson



Slide 23: Exercise 3 - WAR_Season Stripchart
hofpitching <- hof_pitching |>
  mutate(WAR_Season = WAR / Yrs)

ggplot(hofpitching, aes(WAR_Season, BF_group)) + 
  geom_jitter(height = 0.1)


Slide 24: Exercise 3 - WAR_Season Boxplot
ggplot(hofpitching, aes(BF_group, WAR_Season)) + 
  geom_boxplot(fill = "orange", color = "brown") +
  coord_flip()

Interpretation: More batters faced correlates with higher WAR/Season, but with more variability



Slide 25: Exercise 4 - Dot Plot for Post-1960 Pitchers
hofpitching <- hofpitching |>
  mutate(MidYear = (From + To) / 2)

hofpitching_recent <- hofpitching |>
  filter(MidYear >= 1960) |>
  arrange(desc(WAR_Season))

ggplot(hofpitching_recent, aes(x = WAR_Season, y = fct_reorder(Name, WAR_Season))) + 
  geom_point(color = "darkgreen")

Top 2 standout pitchers: Roger Clemens, Pedro Martinez



Slide 26: Exercise 5 - WAR_Season vs. MidYear
ggplot(hofpitching, aes(MidYear, WAR_Season)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_text(data = filter(hofpitching, MidYear < 1900 & WAR_Season < 3),
            aes(label = Name), color = "red")

Pattern: Slight decline in WAR/Season over time; early pitchers (e.g., 1800s) had lower WAR/Season



Slide 27: Exercise 6 - Cumulative Hits of Cobb, Williams, Rose
# Assumes hits_by_age df with Player, Age, Hits
# Data prep for all 3 players skipped for brevity

ggplot(hits_by_age, aes(Age, Hits, color = Player)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  ylab("Cumulative Hits")

Summary: Rose had the longest consistent hitting career, Cobb peaked earlier, Williams' peak was sharp but interrupted



Slide 28: Exercise 7 - Team ERA vs. Win % (2022)
Teams <- Teams |>
  filter(yearID == 2022) |>
  mutate(win_pct = W / (W + L))

ggplot(Teams, aes(ERA, win_pct)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  xlab("Team ERA") + ylab("Winning Percentage")


Slide 29: Exercise 7 - Logos in Scatterplot (mlbplotR installed)
ggplot(Teams, aes(ERA, win_pct)) +
  geom_mlb_logos(aes(team_abbr = teamID), width = 0.06) +
  xlab("ERA") + ylab("Win %") + ggtitle("ERA vs Win % with Team Logos")


Slide 30: Exercise 8 - Home Run Spacing
HR_Spacing <- bind_rows(
  tibble(Player = "McGwire", Spacing = mac_spacings),
  tibble(Player = "Sosa", Spacing = sosa_spacings)
)

ggplot(HR_Spacing, aes(Spacing, fill = Player)) + 
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.5, binwidth = 1)

Insight: McGwire hit home runs more frequently (shorter average spacing)
